name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us real-world data without disrupting workflows, letting us measure actual impact before committing. The trade-off is delayed immediate feedback, but we avoid breaking contributor trust with premature changes. After two weeks, we’ll have clear metrics to decide if full rollout is worth the risk.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It won’t flag real risks like subtle security gaps or breaking changes because it only sees what passes initial review. Run a controlled A/B test instead: split PRs into two groups—one with PR-Agent active, one without—and measure *actual* failure rates in production, not just shadow logs.
